title: Test Timeout - Preventing Infinite Loops
description: Set a timeout to prevent tests from running forever.

theory.title: Exercise 2.1.5: Test Timeout
theory.content:
⏱️ Time Limits for Safety

MENTOR-9: "PROTO-7, imagine a test gets stuck waiting for a response that never comes. Or an infinite loop in your code. Without a timeout, it runs FOREVER."

"Test Timeout sets a maximum execution time for each test. Exceed it? Test fails immediately. It's a critical safety mechanism."

⏰ What is Test Timeout?

Test Timeout - Maximum time allowed for each test to complete

  • ✅ Prevents hanging tests: Auto-fail if test runs too long
  • ✅ Catches infinite loops: Stop runaway code
  • ✅ Ensures predictable runtime: Test suite won't hang forever
  • ✅ Per-test application: Each test gets its own timeout

When to Use Timeout:

  • 🔹 Network operations: API calls, web requests
  • 🔹 Long-running processes: File uploads, data processing
  • 🔹 External dependencies: Database queries, third-party services
  • 🔹 Development safety: Catch infinite loops during debugging

📝 Test Timeout Example

*** Settings ***
Test Timeout    10 seconds

*** Test Cases ***
Fast Test
    Log    This completes in 1 second
    # ✅ Passes - under 10 seconds

Slow Test
    Sleep    15 seconds
    Log    This takes too long
    # ❌ Fails - exceeds 10 seconds timeout

Time Units Supported:

  • 🔹 30 seconds or 30s or 30 sec
  • 🔹 5 minutes or 5min or 5m
  • 🔹 1 hour or 1h
  • 🔹 2 days or 2d

📋 Test Timeout Rules

  • 🔹 Syntax: Test Timeout 30 seconds
  • 🔹 Applies to: EVERY test case in the suite
  • 🔹 Failure: Test fails with "Test timeout exceeded" message
  • 🔹 Override: Individual tests can override with [Timeout] setting
  • 🔹 Default: No timeout if not specified (can run forever)

🎯 Your Task

Create a suite with Test Timeout set to 30 seconds. Add two quick tests - they'll complete well within the limit, so both will pass.
